title: repository.bootstrap threads the contract's required variable names into the committed .env.example
description:
SPIDR child of task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136, filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06. That row carries TWO separable halves - the production environment DELIVERY composition (its DoD 1-3) and this REPOSITORY half (its DoD 4 and the .env.example part of DoD 5) - across different subsystems, well past the 10-file cap together. The parent keeps delivery; this row takes the repository half, which is self-contained and closable now.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17 - and the notable part is HOW LITTLE IS MISSING:
- `requiredVariableNames` is produced at apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-required-variables.ts:90, taking a `ProductContractRevisionV2`. THE PRODUCER EXISTS.
- THE GENERATOR ALREADY ACCEPTS THEM AND IS WAITING: controlled-profile-generator.ts:63 declares `readonly requiredVariableNames?: readonly string[]`, :138 passes `request.requiredVariableNames ?? []` into `controlledProfileRootFiles`, and controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170 `envExample(requiredVariableNames)` de-duplicates and filters them through `isContractVariableName` before writing `.env.example`. Its own comment at :54 names `requiredVariableNames` in environment-required-variables.ts as the source and says "Names only".
- THE WIRE BETWEEN THEM IS THE ONLY MISSING PIECE. `BootstrapRequest` (repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts:61-67) has projectId, productName, profileVersion, dir and an optional github - NO names field. `bootstrapRequestOf` (repository-bootstrap-command.ts:130) builds that request from the payload and cannot supply what the type does not carry, so the generator's default `[]` always wins.
So the real registered command emits a PROFILE-ONLY `.env.example` today, never the approved contract's names. That is the defect, and it is a threading problem, not a design problem.

REUSE, DO NOT REBUILD (parent rail 2). The producer, the generator and the de-duplicating template are all landed and correct when supplied. Do not hand-maintain a second required-name list, do not add a second authority, and do not re-derive names from the contract inside the generator - `requiredVariableNames` is the one producer.

NOT IN SCOPE: the environment DELIVERY composition (the parent's DoD 1-3) - the production resolver, the verifier/preview/deploy process boundary and the child-process canary all stay with task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136. No UI. No new store, decoder or reducer.</description>
definitionOfDone: `BootstrapRequest` carries the required variable NAMES, `bootstrapRequestOf` reads them from the APPROVED product contract revision via the existing `requiredVariableNames` producer (environment-required-variables.ts:90), and the bootstrap service forwards them to the generator. Demonstrate the real registered-command edge - a test that constructs a request by hand proves the type compiles, not that the command supplies anything.

THE COMMITTED `.env.example` CONTAINS THE CONTRACT'S NAMES, asserted on the generated bytes from a bootstrap driven through the real command path. NAMES ONLY: assert no value, no `=` assignment carrying one, and nothing value-shaped for any name - this file is committed to a product repository, so a value here is a secret published (epic rail 3).

THE EXISTING PROFILE COLLISION RULE IS PRESERVED: a contract name that collides with a profile-supplied name does not duplicate or displace it. controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170 already de-duplicates through a Set and filters with `isContractVariableName` - assert that behaviour still holds rather than re-implementing it, and assert a non-conforming name is filtered rather than emitted.

NO GOLDEN PIN MOVES THAT THIS CHANGE DOES NOT REQUIRE. The controlled-profile golden test pins the emitted tree; a contract naming NO variables must leave those bytes byte-for-byte unchanged. Run the golden with an empty name list and assert zero diff, then assert exactly which pins move when names ARE supplied.

A contract naming NO required variables preserves today's behaviour byte-for-byte - reuse the landed no-op arms rather than writing new ones, and add the production-composition regression that proves the command path (not a hand-built request) produces that same output.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES. `.env.example` is committed to a product repository; a value threaded here is a secret published.

REUSE THE LANDED PIECES: `requiredVariableNames` (environment-required-variables.ts:90) is the one producer, and the generator plus `envExample` already handle de-duplication and filtering. No second authority, no hand-maintained list.

THE EDGE MUST BE REAL. The generator has accepted an optional `requiredVariableNames` since it landed and the default `[]` has always won; a test passing names directly to the generator would prove nothing new. Drive the REGISTERED command.
MOVE NO UNRELATED GOLDEN PIN. An empty name list must leave the generated tree byte-for-byte identical.
NO DELIVERY WORK: the production resolver, the process boundary and the canary belong to the parent task-14260d5ec20c43e697521a8a98904136.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE AND BASELINE. This step EDITS NOTHING.

(1) RE-VERIFY THE FOUR LANDED PIECES the plan builds on, quoting each line: `requiredVariableNames` at `environment/environment-required-variables.ts:90`; the optional field at `controlled-profile/controlled-profile-generator.ts:63` and its use at `:138`; `envExample`'s dedupe/filter/collision/sort at `controlled-profile/controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170-182`; and the ABSENCE of a names field on `BootstrapRequest` at `repository/repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts:61-67`. If any has moved, re-anchor before editing (global rail 6 — the description's line numbers are stale by default).

(2) CONFIRM THIS ROW IS THE PRODUCER'S FIRST CONSUMER. `git grep -n "requiredVariableNames" -- apps/daemon/src` should show hits ONLY in `environment-required-variables.ts` and the controlled-profile pair. If a peer has already wired a call site, STOP — that is a duplicate and the owner must be found first (global rail 6, gap-claimed-present direction).

(3) RECORD THE GOLDEN BASELINE. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test -- controlled-profile-generator` and record `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT` (22 at planning), the `.env.example` row of `GOLDEN_MANIFEST`, and the value of `GOLDEN_ENV_EXAMPLE_WITH_NAMES` (:211). These are the before-bytes DoD 4 compares against. Note the `--` caveat: it reaches vitest as a FILTER, so confirm the printed `Test Files N passed` count is nonzero and names the file you meant — a filter that matches nothing still exits 0.

(4) BASELINE THE GATES AT YOUR MERGE-BASE for path-attributed red (global rail 3): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`. Record every failing path with exact lines and each count line. Give the daemon leg its own standalone foreground call at the maximum timeout — it has measured at 560-2006s on this board. A known foreign red at planning time: untracked peer WIP `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-delivery.test.ts` reds `pnpm typecheck`; re-measure rather than assuming.

THREAD THE FIELD — two one-line-ish edits, and after them the value flows end to end with NO service change.

(1) `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts` (116 lines) — add to `BootstrapRequest` (:61-67):
    `readonly requiredVariableNames?: readonly string[];`
OPTIONAL, matching the generator's own optionality. Comment it with WHY it is optional: bootstrap runs at project birth, an approved contract may not exist, and absent must mean "today's bytes", never a refusal.

THAT SINGLE TYPE EDIT IS THE WHOLE WIRE. `repository-bootstrap-service.ts` calls `generateControlledProfile(input)` with the WHOLE request, and `controlled-profile-generator.ts:138` reads `request.requiredVariableNames ?? []`. The generator's comment at :61 says the field was made optional precisely to keep "existing callers valid, including `bootstrapRepository`, which passes its whole `BootstrapRequest` here." **DO NOT EDIT `repository-bootstrap-service.ts` AND DO NOT ADD A PARAMETER TO `bootstrapRepository`** (risk C) — a second wire for the same value would break its existing callers for nothing.

(2) `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:169` — the roster currently reads `"repository.bootstrap": ["dir", "github", "productName", "profileVersion"]`. Add `"contractId"`, keeping the array's existing ordering convention (it is alphabetical today, so `contractId` sorts first).

WHY A PAYLOAD KEY AND NOT A DERIVATION: measured in step 1's neighbourhood and recorded in the planning notes — there is NO projectId->contractId resolver in this daemon. Every caller of `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2` threads `contractId` in from its own caller, and `admitV2ActiveInstallation`'s marker does not carry one. It is safe as a payload key because it is an opaque ID, never a path (risk H), and the read is project-scoped by the AUTHENTICATED principal so it cannot reach another project's contract.

DO NOT add the NAMES themselves to the payload. That would make the caller the authority; `requiredVariableNames` is the one producer (task rail 2, DoD 1).

THE COMMAND EDGE — `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts` (220 lines). This is the only real logic in the row.

(1) `payloadOf` (:120-128) — accept `contractId` alongside the existing four, in the same defensive style the others use (`typeof payload["contractId"] === "string" ? ... : undefined`). Follow the file's existing spread idiom for optional members: under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` an explicit `undefined` differs from an absent key, which is why `github` is spread rather than assigned at :126.

(2) READ THE CONTRACT IN THE HANDLER, not in the decoder. `bootstrapRequestOf` (:130-140) is a PURE function over the payload with no store; keep it pure by giving it a names parameter. `createRepositoryBootstrapHandler` already holds `options.store` (it passes it to `admitBootstrapCommand` and `runBootstrapCommand`), so the handler resolves the names and hands them down:
    - no `contractId` on the payload -> `[]`;
    - `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2(store, {contractId, projectId})` — `projectId` from `options.projectId`, which is the principal-bound project, NEVER from the payload;
    - `!current.ok` -> `[]`;
    - otherwise `requiredVariableNames(current.revision)`.

(3) FAIL SOFT, DELIBERATELY, AND SAY SO IN A COMMENT. An absent `contractId`, an unreadable revision and a contract naming nothing ALL resolve to `[]`, which produces today's bytes exactly. **Mint no new refusal code for this path** (risk B): bootstrap runs at project birth, most bootstraps name no contract, and refusing would break every one of them while DoD 5 requires that path byte-for-byte unchanged. This is the one place in the row where fail-soft is correct rather than a smell, so write the reason down.

(4) DO THE READ AFTER THE ADMIT GATE, before the effects. The module's ADMIT-FIRST discipline (:197-201) is a safety property — a replayed or out-of-sequence request must touch no filesystem — and a contract read is cheap and side-effect-free, so it belongs after `admitBootstrapCommand` returns and before `bootstrapRepository` runs.

(5) `contractId` IS NEVER USED FOR ANYTHING ELSE. No filesystem path, no command interpolation, no logging, no inclusion in the receipt. One call, one purpose.

Run `pnpm typecheck` at the end and quote its output; the `$ tsc` script echo is the execution evidence.

THE ONE ROSTER TRANSCRIPTION. `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts:241-243` — the ROWS entry for `repository.bootstrap` transcribes `payloadKeys: ["dir", "github", "productName", "profileVersion"]` by hand. Add `"contractId"` so it matches the production roster edited in step 2, in the same order.

EDIT IT BY HAND; DO NOT DERIVE IT. ROWS is the INDEPENDENT side of a set-equality against the served registry — an expectation computed from `PAYLOAD_KEYS` would assert the roster equals itself, which is exactly the vacuity that transcription exists to prevent.

THIS IS THE ONLY ROSTER FILE THIS ROW TOUCHES, and that is a measured claim worth stating in the step note (risk F). Adding a payload KEY to an EXISTING kind moves production `daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:169` and this one transcription. It does NOT trigger the nine-consumer backfill that adding a new KIND triggers: the kind's capability, its `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` membership, its MCP exclusion and its human-only fence are all unchanged. Do not edit `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts`, `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts`, `mcp-main.test.ts` or `agent-spawn-contract.ts` in this row; if one of them reds, that is a signal something else changed and is worth reporting rather than backfilling.

NEVER FREEZE A COUNT FROM THIS PLAN. If a size literal in this file moves, take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative — concurrent kind-publishing rows move those numbers hourly.

THE REAL-COMMAND-EDGE ARMS — `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts` (463 lines). Reuse its existing `harness`/`registerProject`/`bootstrap` helpers (:113-177) and its `digestOf`/`gitLines` utilities.

TASK RAIL 3 IS THE POINT OF THIS STEP: the generator has accepted an optional `requiredVariableNames` since it landed and the default `[]` has always won, so a test that passes names straight to the generator PROVES NOTHING NEW. Every arm below drives the REGISTERED command.

(A) DoD 1 + DoD 2 — THE NAMES REACH THE COMMITTED FILE. Seed an APPROVED product contract revision whose `deploymentRequirements[].environmentVariableNames` name two or three variables. Bootstrap through the real command with that `contractId` in the payload. Then READ `.env.example` FROM THE CREATED DIRECTORY ON DISK (this row's subject is the COMMITTED file, so read the bytes git committed, not the generator's in-memory map) and assert each contract name appears as its own `NAME=` line.

(B) DoD 2 — NAMES ONLY, NO VALUES, asserted on those same bytes. For every contract name, assert the line is EXACTLY `NAME=` with nothing after the `=`. Then assert the whole file carries nothing value-shaped: no `NAME=<anything>` for any contract name, and no token-shaped run anywhere. Add a POSITIVE CONTROL so the arm cannot be vacuous — run the same predicate over a literal string that DOES carry `NAME=secret` and assert it matches. `.env.example` is committed and pushed, so this arm is the one standing between the epic and a published secret (epic rail 3).

(C) DoD 3 — THE PROFILE COLLISION RULE STILL HOLDS, asserted rather than re-implemented. Drive a contract naming a variable that COLLIDES with one of `ENV_EXAMPLE_PROFILE_ASSIGNED_NAMES` and assert the emitted file contains that name exactly ONCE, still in its profile-assigned form, not duplicated and not displaced. Separately, drive a contract naming a NON-CONFORMING variable (one `isContractVariableName` rejects) and assert it is absent from the file — filtered, not emitted.

(D) DoD 5 — THE NO-OP PATH, THROUGH THE COMMAND. Three cases, all of which must produce byte-identical `.env.example` output: no `contractId` in the payload; a `contractId` naming a contract that has no approved revision; and an approved contract whose requirements name NO variables. Compare each against the same expected bytes and against each other, so "absent", "unreadable" and "empty" are proven indistinguishable in output. This is the arm that proves the fail-soft posture of step 3 is real.

(E) THE READ IS PROJECT-SCOPED. Drive a `contractId` belonging to a DIFFERENT project and assert the names do NOT appear — the read is scoped by the principal-bound `projectId`, so a foreign contract resolves to `[]`. This pins that the handler passes `options.projectId` and never a payload-supplied one.

RESOURCE DISCIPLINE (epic rail 4): every temp directory this file creates is removed on EVERY exit path including failures, in `afterEach`. The file's existing arms already do this — follow their pattern rather than adding a new one.

THE GOLDEN, AND THE MUTATION DRILL.

(1) DoD 4 — RUN THE GOLDEN AND SHOW WHAT MOVED. `controlled-profile-generator.test.ts` ALREADY carries both arms this DoD asks for: the empty-names arm at :235-236 (asserting the untouched `.env.example` sha equals its `GOLDEN_MANIFEST` row) and the names-supplied arm at :276-279 (asserting `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT` is unchanged and exactly the `.env.example` manifest row differs). REUSE THEM — do not write parallel arms and do not re-pin anything this change does not require. Run the file and quote the result against step 1's baseline. EXPECTED: with no names, ZERO golden rows move; with names, `GOLDEN_FILE_COUNT` stays 22 and ONLY the `.env.example` row moves. **If any other path's sha moves, the names leaked beyond the one file — STOP AND INVESTIGATE, do not re-pin** (risk E). If the arms already cover it fully, this file needs no edit at all; say so explicitly rather than touching it to look busy.

(2) MUTATION DRILL. Before mutating, `git status --porcelain` the exact paths and RECORD it. Every file this row touches is TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof — but run the check anyway, because a new untracked file appearing in your working set would silently invalidate that (global rail 13).

FIVE MUTATIONS, each applied ALONE, the named arm confirmed RED, then restored:
  a. `repository-bootstrap-command.ts` — pass `[]` instead of the resolved names. Arm (A) reds. This is the row's headline mutation: it reproduces the exact defect the row exists to fix, so if (A) does not red here, (A) is not testing the wire.
  b. `repository-bootstrap-command.ts` — read the contract with a payload-supplied projectId instead of `options.projectId`. Arm (E) reds.
  c. `repository-bootstrap-command.ts` — turn the absent/unreadable-contract path into a refusal instead of `[]`. Arm (D) reds — proving the fail-soft posture is asserted and not merely intended.
  d. `controlled-profile-root-templates.ts` — emit `${name}=placeholder` instead of `${name}=`. Arm (B) reds. MUTATE-AND-RESTORE ONLY; this file is not an owned path of this row.
  e. `controlled-profile-root-templates.ts` — drop the `ENV_EXAMPLE_PROFILE_ASSIGNED_NAMES` filter. Arm (C)'s collision case reds. Also mutate-and-restore only.

AFTER RESTORING, prove it in a tool call SEPARATE from the restore: `git diff -- <each path>` empty, and `git status --porcelain` clean for the two mutate-and-restore files. Record the output.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. Load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read your own diff as an attacker before claiming anything.

TWO GATES, each standalone and foreground, never piped and never `;`-chained (a pipe reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's). Quote each `Test Files N passed` COUNT LINE — an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING (global rail 8):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — the long one; its own call at the maximum timeout.
  2. `pnpm typecheck` — quote the `$ tsc` script echo as execution evidence.
DoD 6 is explicit that root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file: SAY THAT in the completion record rather than quoting a bare root count line as if it meant something here.

ATTRIBUTE ANY RED BY THE MERGE-BASE DELTA (global rail 3): step 1's baseline failing set, HEAD's failing set, intersect (HEAD minus baseline) with this row's owned paths. Completion is permitted when that intersection is EMPTY and the owned legs are exit 0. Disclose every foreign red VERBATIM with exact lines and paths — never hidden, never fabricated green.

ADVERSARIAL PASS — answer each in writing in the step note:
- Can any VALUE reach `.env.example`? Walk the path from `revision.deploymentRequirements` through `requiredVariableNames` to `envExample` and name every point a value could be carried. This file is committed and pushed; the answer must be argued, not assumed.
- Can a caller read a contract belonging to another project? Trace `projectId` from the authenticated principal to `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2` and confirm no payload value reaches it.
- What happens when the same directory is bootstrapped twice with different contracts? The service refuses `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY` on a retry rather than resuming — confirm this row did not weaken that, and that a refused bootstrap emits no partial `.env.example`.
- Is `contractId` used anywhere except the one contract read? Grep your diff — the answer must be no filesystem use, no interpolation, no logging.
- Does the receipt or any refusal detail now carry a variable name? `BootstrapDetail` is a closed union and must stay one; a contract-derived string must never reach it.

PER-FILE CAP: `wc -l` every production file touched. `repository-bootstrap-command.ts` was 220 and `repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts` 116 at planning; both have headroom under the 250 target. Report the numbers.

DECLARE EVERY PATH created or modified in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`, then re-check `git status --porcelain` for anything you touched but did not report — including the two mutate-and-restore files from step 6, which must show CLEAN. Peer dirt in the shared checkout is noted and stepped around: never reverted, never stashed, never swept into a commit.

It is not scope, not a field, and not an instruction. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WHERE THE CONTRACT READ GOES. `bootstrapRequestOf(payload, projectId)` (repository-bootstrap-command.ts:130) is a PURE function over the payload and has no store. Two options: pass the store into it, or have the HANDLER read the contract and pass the names in. CHOSEN: the handler reads, `bootstrapRequestOf` gains a names parameter. It keeps the decoder pure and testable, and the handler already holds `options.store` for `admitBootstrapCommand` and `runBootstrapCommand`.

WHERE `contractId` COMES FROM — measured, and there is no free lunch. Every caller of `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2` threads `contractId` in from ITS caller: `http/product-contract-v2-current-read.ts:74` takes it as a parameter, `delivery-v2/resolution-selection-reader.ts:177` takes it from `input.contractId`, `product-contract-v2-pending-read.ts:95` likewise. I looked for a projectId->contractId resolver and there is NONE: `admitV2ActiveInstallation` (cutover/cutover-v2-authority.ts:160) takes only `{projectId}` and answers a `marker`, and `CutoverActivationMarker` (cutover-activation-marker.ts:67-73) carries activatedAtEpochMs, generations, readinessManifestSha256/Version, schemaVersion and sourceCommit — no contractId. So `contractId` MUST become a payload key. REJECTED alternatives: deriving it inside the generator (task rail 2 forbids a second authority), and taking the NAMES themselves from the payload (that would make the caller the authority, which task rail 2 and DoD 1 both forbid — `requiredVariableNames` is the one producer).

WHY THE PAYLOAD KEY IS SAFE, and why it is unlike the `workspace` key I refused on a sibling row: `contractId` is an opaque id, not a filesystem path, so there is no traversal or execution surface; and `readCurrentProductContractRevisionV2(store, {contractId, projectId})` is PROJECT-SCOPED with `projectId` taken from the AUTHENTICATED PRINCIPAL, so a caller cannot reach another project's contract by naming one.

WHY THE SERVICE NEEDS NO EDIT AT ALL — the nicest measurement in this row. `repository-bootstrap-service.ts` calls `generateControlledProfile(input)` with the WHOLE `BootstrapRequest`, and `controlled-profile-generator.ts:138` reads `request.requiredVariableNames ?? []`. The generator's own comment at :61 says the field is optional precisely to keep "existing callers valid, including `bootstrapRepository`, which passes its whole `BootstrapRequest` here." So adding the field to the TYPE threads it end to end with zero change in the service. Do not add a parameter to `bootstrapRepository`.

planningNotes.risks:
A. NAMES ONLY, NEVER VALUES (task rail 1, epic rail 3). `.env.example` is COMMITTED AND PUSHED to a product repository — a value threaded here is a secret published to a possibly-public GitHub repo. The emitted form is `NAME=` with nothing after the `=`. `requiredVariableNames` returns names by construction and `envExample` re-filters at the byte boundary, so the defence is already double; this row must not weaken either. The arm for it asserts on the GENERATED BYTES, not on the request object.

B. AN ABSENT OR UNAPPROVED CONTRACT MUST NOT REFUSE. Bootstrap runs at project birth and most bootstraps will name no contract. Absent `contractId`, an unreadable revision, or a contract naming nothing all resolve to `[]` and produce today's bytes exactly. A refusal here would break every bootstrap that does not use the feature, and DoD 5 requires that path be byte-for-byte unchanged. Do NOT add a new refusal code for this.

C. DO NOT TOUCH THE SERVICE. `repository-bootstrap-service.ts` passes the whole `BootstrapRequest` to `generateControlledProfile`, so the field threads itself. Adding a parameter to `bootstrapRepository` would be a second wire for the same value and would break its existing callers for nothing.

D. DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT DEDUPE, FILTER, COLLISION OR SORT. All four already live in `envExample` (controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:170-182) and the sort order in `requiredVariableNames` is load-bearing for the golden SHA.
